response: {"title":"One assertion per requirement","intervention":"Represent every explicit requirement with at least one focused automated assertion and make those assertions pass before declaring completion.","claim":"On matched fixed-deadline Python tasks with dispersed requirements, this appended instruction will produce a higher complete pass_rate than no appended instruction while keeping median wall_time and turns within 15% of control.","mechanism":"Requiring a concrete assertion for each requirement turns vague completion judgments into executable coverage signals that expose omissions and cross-module integration failures.","assumptions":["Each explicit requirement has behavior that can be asserted within the available test harness.","Focused assertions can be written and run within the deadline."],"risks":["The agent may write weak assertions that mirror its implementation and miss the intended behavior.","Test construction may consume time needed for implementation.","Nonfunctional requirements may not map cleanly to automated assertions."],"test_plan":{"experiment":"Randomly assign matched multi-module Python tasks and fixed deadlines to the appended instruction or no-instruction control, then grade both with an independent hidden suite.","metrics":["pass_rate","wall_time","turns"],"success_condition":"Treatment complete-task pass_rate is higher, with treatment median wall_time and turns each no more than 115% of control."},"single_shot_ordinal":7}
